topFixes: Make the 3D asset the first investment. Blurred skin shading, visible seams, thin shell-like cut surfaces and crude internal geometry make this look like a prototype beside BioDigital. Improve meshes, section caps, material differentiation and lighting before polishing UI chrome.

Replace blanket X-ray transparency with selective isolation. The selected clitoris and uterus views contain a confusing tangle of translucent structures. Keep the selected organ opaque, ghost only essential anatomical context and hide unrelated geometry. 'On its own' should actually look isolated.

Constrain the desktop camera to the unobstructed canvas between the toolbar and inspector. The selected clitoris view balloons behind the heading and panels and crops important context. Fit each selection deliberately, including its labels.

Recompose mobile around the anatomical focal point. First load spends too much height on the upper skin surface while the useful anatomy sits low. Reduce the tour button's dominance, compact the header and center the relevant structures in the available viewport.

Upgrade callouts from small boxed captions to a coherent annotation system: consistent label columns, collision-aware leader lines, larger invisible hit targets and fewer simultaneous labels. Preserve context without covering the model with badges.

Separate primary exploration from simulation controls. Keep views and part selection prominent; put arousal, X-ray and contraction playback in a clearly labeled secondary group. 'Slice across' versus 'Side cut' needs clearer differentiation.

Give mobile detail sheets deliberate collapsed, half-height and expanded states. The uterus sheet obscures much of the model, while its bottom fade washes out text. Reframe the organ above the sheet and provide a clearer continuation cue; retain an explicit active view or isolation state.

Push the manual identity beyond bold headings and default panels. Unify numbering, captions, rules, spacing and icon strokes into a more precise editorial system. Break the mobile reference section into compact illustrated comparisons rather than a long, visually monotonous table.
